hints: Look closely at the structure. A triglyceride has glycerol + 3 fatty acids, but a phospholipid replaces one fatty acid with a phosphate. How many of each does one phospholipid have?
Remember it is condensation just like triglyceride formation. Count how many ester bonds form in one phospholipid, so how many water molecules ($18 g mol^{-1}$) must you subtract?
walkthrough:
**Picture one phospholipid**

Think side by side with me. A triglyceride is glycerol + 3 fatty acids joined by 3 ester bonds.

A phospholipid is very similar, but it is glycerol + 2 fatty acids + 1 phosphate. That is still 3 bonds in total.

**Calculate the mass of one phospholipid**

Add the parts together, then subtract the water lost in condensation. Each ester bond releases one water.

$$Mass = glycerol + (2 \times fatty\ acid) + phosphate - (3 \times water)$$
$$Mass = 92 + (2 \times 282) + 95 - (3 \times 18)$$
$$Mass = 92 + 564 + 95 - 54 = 697\ g\ mol^{-1}$$

**Scale up to the whole sample**

The sample has six identical phospholipid molecules, so multiply by 6.

$$Sample\ mass = 6 \times 697 = 4182\ g\ mol^{-1}$$

options.A: Too low. This uses only 1 fatty acid per phospholipid, but a phospholipid has 2 fatty acids plus 1 phosphate.
options.B: Correct. One phospholipid is 697 g mol-1, and 6 x 697 = 4182 g mol-1 after subtracting 3 waters for condensation.
options.C: Too high. This adds all parts (751 x 6) but forgets to subtract the 3 water molecules lost in condensation.
options.D: Too high. This adds the water instead of subtracting it, which is the opposite of what happens in condensation.
